{"duplicatePairs":[
{"a":"V21-B01-S00-BC-01","b":"V21-B03-S00-BC-01","reason":"Both are the inherited decades-old family hardware store whose loyal older trade customers value the unchanged, old-fashioned feel while younger customers find it dated/intimidating, with a single name and no option to run two identities — the identical brand-positioning decision differing only in store age and whether a second site is mentioned."},
{"a":"V21-B01-S00-BC-01","b":"V21-B05-S00-BC-01","reason":"Both are a long-established neighbourhood retailer keeping its product, premises and prices unchanged and asking only how signage/voice/presentation should evolve to convert a younger incoming demographic into regulars without losing the older loyalists who cite the old-fashioned feel as the reason they trust it. Same decision, hardware swapped for deli."},
{"a":"V21-B02-S00-BC-01","b":"V21-B04-S00-BC-01","reason":"Both are a decades-old technical/utilitarian apparel maker whose core rugged user base fears dilution while ~40-45% of revenue has shifted to urban professionals who find the technical voice cold or aggressive; both ask for a positioning and tonal framework that bridges heritage credibility with urban lifestyle appeal under one brand. Identical decision, workwear vs alpine wear."},
{"a":"V21-B01-S00-EI-01","b":"V21-B05-S00-EI-01","reason":"Both present a retention improvement following a new program that is confounded by two co-timed changes — a price/pay increase and a tightening of intake criteria that selects for people who would have stayed anyway — and ask what the data actually attributes to the program before a decision to roll it out organisation-wide. Same causal-attribution decision with school swapped for hospital."},
{"a":"V21-B03-S00-EI-02","b":"V21-B05-S00-EI-02","reason":"Both compare a policy piloted in a subset of institutions against the non-pilot remainder, where the pilot sites were non-equivalent (co-occurring curriculum/renovation advantages, comparison sites declining), with a board treating the gap as proof and pushing system-wide expansion; both ask what the data really shows about causation. Same decision, four-day week vs late-fee elimination."},
{"a":"V21-B03-S00-FR-01","b":"V21-B05-S00-FR-01","reason":"Both are an unrestricted one-time bequest from a longtime donor's estate that must be split among exactly three claims — an urgent-but-not-immediate roof repair with a stated deadline, an education/tutoring program facing a funding cliff, and a third institutional need — with no way to fund all three. Same allocation decision, different sum and organisation."},
{"a":"V21-B01-S00-FR-01","b":"V21-B04-S00-FR-01","reason":"Both are a cultural institution dividing a one-time capital fund that must be committed before a deadline across the same three claim types: an urgent building-fabric failure threatening the collection/closure, a physical expansion serving new audiences, and a digitisation project that unlocks external research/licensing income. Identical allocation trade-off, museum vs library."},
{"a":"V21-B02-S00-FR-02","b":"V21-B04-S00-FR-02","reason":"Both allocate a fixed, pre-approved block of new engineering-side headcount across department requests that substantially exceed it, with the same competing justifications (revenue/SLA risk, delivery backlog blocking recognised revenue, platform/next-gen work), asking for a distribution and its trade-off rationale. Same headcount-rationing decision."},
{"a":"V21-B01-S00-FR-02","b":"V21-B05-S00-FR-02","reason":"Both divide a fixed discretionary budget among exactly three departmental requests totalling roughly $35-45k more than available, where one request is replacing equipment that failed twice recently, one promises revenue/efficiency upside, and one addresses an ongoing cost or obligation, with a decision due at an imminent meeting. Same allocation decision, theatre vs plant."},
{"a":"V21-B01-S00-OP-02","b":"V21-B02-S00-OP-01","reason":"Both take an already-approved healthcare IT system rollout and ask only for the execution sequence across sites, constrained by being able to take/support one site at a time, a limited pool of trainers/staff who cannot all be released at once, and a hard external deadline. Same sequencing problem at different scale."},
{"a":"V21-B01-S00-OP-01","b":"V21-B02-S00-OP-02","reason":"Both are a bakery with signed new supermarket wholesale contracts (volume fixed, decision final) asking how to schedule mixing/proofing/baking across limited ovens and staff so the new wholesale volume is met alongside existing commitments. Same production-scheduling decision, differing only in the numbers and whether delivery legs are included."},
{"a":"V21-B04-S00-OP-02","b":"V21-B05-S00-OP-02","reason":"Both are a food/beverage producer committed to a fixed contracted volume delivered in staggered batch shipments, scheduling a multi-stage process (fermentation/setting times, single or dual constrained lines with changeover/sanitation, limited holding capacity with spoilage or storage caps) to hit each milestone without gaps. Same scheduling decision."},
{"a":"V21-B02-S00-PS-01","b":"V21-B04-S00-PS-01","reason":"Both are a multi-site workspace operator with hybrid-driven peak/trough occupancy designing a corporate membership product for distributed teams, asked to define tiers, credit/entitlement mechanics, meeting-room booking rules and admin/access controls while smoothing utilisation and protecting existing occupants. Same product-design decision, co-working chain vs office-tower landlord."},
{"a":"V21-B02-S00-PS-02","b":"V21-B04-S00-PS-02","reason":"Both are a multi-location dental group designing an in-house membership plan for uninsured patients to replace fee-for-service, asked to specify tiers, included preventive care, discount mechanics on restorative work, frequency limits and membership terms without eroding margin. Same design decision, adult general practice vs pediatric."},
{"a":"V21-B01-S00-PS-01","b":"V21-B02-S00-PS-02","reason":"Both are a clinical practice that has decided to replace unpredictable pay-per-visit billing with a subscription/membership for routine care and now must define what it covers, how many tiers, and how to cap exposure on unpredictable higher-cost treatment given fixed clinical capacity. Same offer-design decision, veterinary vs dental."},
{"a":"V21-B03-S00-SC-01","b":"V21-B05-S00-SC-01","reason":"Both are the same 14-person structural engineering firm, eight years subcontracting to two general contractors, weighing the same $600k offer for a 40% stake (board seat, exclusivity tying them to that contractor's pipeline) against a debt-funded independent growth move, with both offers expiring at month-end and an explicit clause preventing doing both."},
{"a":"V21-B02-S00-SC-02","b":"V21-B04-S00-SC-01","reason":"Both are a regional cold-chain logistics operator with capital capacity for only one move, choosing between staying with the established, labour-heavy legacy facility/asset and committing the full capital to build a new automated cold-storage hub whose automation cuts labour costs but yields no revenue during a long build and disrupts staff. Same either/or capital decision."},
{"a":"V21-B04-S00-SC-02","b":"V21-B05-S00-SC-02","reason":"Both are a founder team at the end of runway choosing irreversibly between handing the business/technology to a larger incumbent for immediate cash and certainty while surrendering control and scale-back of the team, versus taking a fresh investor round to build out their own manufacturing/delivery and commercialise independently at higher execution risk, with a board/investor deadline days away."},
{"a":"V21-B01-S00-SC-01","b":"V21-B02-S00-SC-01","reason":"Both are a specialist services/manufacturing firm forced to commit by a near deadline to one of two mutually exclusive paths: a guaranteed multi-year anchor contract with an exclusivity clause that locks out a whole client segment and dedicates core capacity, versus a lower-certainty, diversified path that preserves independence and a broader customer base. Same strategic trade-off."}
]}
